title: The risk of lower gastrointestinal bleeding in low‐dose aspirin users

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Summary</jats:title><jats:sec><jats:title>Background</jats:title><jats:p>Aspirin increases the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Aim</jats:title><jats:p>To investigate the risk of lower gastrointestinal bleeding (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">LGIB</jats:styled-content>) in aspirin users.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Methods</jats:title><jats:p>Low‐dose (75‐325 mg daily) aspirin users and controls matched by age, gender and enrollment time in a 1:5 ratio were selected from 1 million randomly sampled subjects in the National Health Insurance Research Database of Taiwan. Cox proportional hazard regression models were developed to evaluate the predictors of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">LGIB</jats:styled-content> with adjustments for age, gender, comorbidities including coronary artery disease, ischaemic stroke, diabetes, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, liver cirrhosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, dyslipidemia, uncomplicated peptic ulcer disease, history of peptic ulcer bleeding, and concomitant use of clopidogrel, ticlopidine, warfarin, nonsteroidal anti‐inflammatory drugs (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">NSAID</jats:styled-content>s), cyclooxygenase‐2 inhibitors, steroids, proton pump inhibitors (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content>s), histamine‐2 receptor antagonists (H2<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">RA</jats:styled-content>s), nitrates, alendronate, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SSRI</jats:styled-content>s) and calcium channel blockers.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Results</jats:title><jats:p>A total of 53 805 aspirin users and 269 025 controls were included. Aspirin group had a higher incidence of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">LGIB</jats:styled-content> within 1 year than control group (0.20% vs 0.06%, <jats:italic>P</jats:italic><.0001). Aspirin (hazard ratio [<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">HR</jats:styled-content>]: 2.75, 95% confidence interval [<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content>]: 2.06‐3.65), <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">NSAID</jats:styled-content>s (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">HR</jats:styled-content>: 8.61, 95% <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content>: 3.28‐22.58), steroids (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">HR</jats:styled-content>: 10.50, 95% <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content>: 1.98‐55.57), <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SSRI</jats:styled-content>s (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">HR</jats:styled-content>: 11.71, 95% <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content>: 1.40‐97.94), <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content>s (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">HR</jats:styled-content>: 8.47, 95% <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content>: 2.26‐31.71), and H2<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">RA</jats:styled-content>s (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">HR</jats:styled-content>: 10.83, 95% <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content>: 2.98‐39.33) were significantly associated with <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">LGIB</jats:styled-content>.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title><jats:p>The risk of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">LGIB</jats:styled-content> was higher in low‐dose aspirin users than in aspirin nonusers in this nationwide cohort. Low‐dose aspirin, <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">NSAID</jats:styled-content>s, steroids, <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SSRI</jats:styled-content>s, <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">PPI</jats:styled-content>s and H2<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">RA</jats:styled-content>s were independent risk factors for <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">LGIB</jats:styled
